title: The Empty Pool at 5 A.M.: The Unseen Work Behind an Athlete's Medal
title_zh: 清晨五点的空泳池：运动员奖牌背后看不见的付出
intro_zh: 本文约 571 词，包含约 6 个 CET-4 核心词，句子难度适中，适合四级阅读训练。

paragraphs.en: At 4:50 a.m., most city streets are still dark. Inside a swimming center, however, the lights are already on. A young swimmer stands at the edge of the pool, adjusting her goggles. By 5:00, she is in the water, moving through lane after lane while the stands remain empty. The race that made her famous on television lasted just 58 seconds. The work behind it has lasted years.
paragraphs.zh: 清晨4点50分，大多数城市街道仍然漆黑。然而在一座游泳中心里，灯已经亮了。一名年轻游泳运动员站在池边，调整着泳镜。到5点时，她已入水，在一条又一条泳道中穿行，而看台依然空无一人。那场让她在电视上成名的比赛只持续了58秒。而它背后的付出已持续多年。

paragraphs.en: Fans see the final moment: the touch of the wall, the scoreboard, the smile. What they do not see is the repetition. An elite swimmer may train 20 to 25 hours a week, about 1,000 hours a year. During that time, one turn at the wall can be practiced thousands of times. Coaches use video to check a wrist angle or a breath. A tiny change may save only 0.05 seconds, but at the top level, that is the difference between first and fourth place.
paragraphs.zh: 观众看到的是最后一刻：触壁、记分牌、微笑。他们看不到的是重复。一名精英游泳运动员每周可能训练20到25小时，一年约1000小时。那段时间里，一个转身动作可能被练习数千次。教练用视频检查手腕角度或呼吸。一个微小的改变也许只能节省0.05秒，但在顶级水平，这就是第一名和第四名之间的差别。

paragraphs.en: This kind of persistence is not romantic. It is often boring. A basketball player may stay after team practice to shoot 200 free throws. A gymnast may repeat the same landing until her legs feel like wood. The body learns through technique, not luck. Each small correction is stored in muscle memory, ready for the moment when the crowd is loud and the hands are shaking.
paragraphs.zh: 这种坚持并不浪漫，往往很枯燥。一名篮球运动员可能在全队训练结束后留下来投200个罚球。一名体操运动员可能重复同一个落地动作，直到双腿像木头一样。身体靠技术学习，而不是靠运气。每一个小小的纠正都存入肌肉记忆，为观众喧闹、双手发抖的那一刻做好准备。

paragraphs.en: Rest is part of the job, too. Many athletes aim for nine to ten hours of sleep, plus short naps. They ice sore knees, stretch tight shoulders, and follow meal plans that can feel strict. Recovery is not a sign of weakness. It is how the body repairs itself and gets ready for the next session. A missed night of sleep can slow reaction time and raise the risk of injury. Going to bed on time becomes a serious choice, not a lazy one.
paragraphs.zh: 休息也是工作的一部分。许多运动员以每晚九到十小时睡眠为目标，外加短暂午睡。他们冰敷酸痛的膝盖，拉伸紧绷的肩膀，遵循可能很严格的饮食计划。恢复不是软弱的表现。它是身体自我修复、为下一次训练做好准备的方式。少睡一夜会减慢反应时间，增加受伤风险。因此，按时上床睡觉成了一个严肃的选择，而不是懒惰的选择。

paragraphs.en: There are darker days, too. Injuries can take months away from the sport. One runner I read about broke a bone in her foot and had to learn to walk again before she could run. She kept a notebook of small goals: stand for ten minutes, walk to the door, jog for one minute. Progress was slow and uneven. Her endurance grew not only in her legs but also in her mind.
paragraphs.zh: 也有更灰暗的日子。伤病可能让人离开运动数月。我读到过一名跑步运动员脚部骨折，在能跑之前不得不重新学走路。她用一个笔记本记下小目标：站立十分钟、走到门口、慢跑一分钟。进展缓慢且不均衡。她的耐力不仅长在腿上，也长在心里。

paragraphs.en: Behind every athlete is a team: coaches, doctors, family, and friends. They drive to early practices, cook meals, and offer comfort after a bad day. Yet on the starting line, the athlete stands alone. That is why the quiet work matters. The crowd can cheer, but it cannot take the final step for you. The athlete must decide, again and again, to show up when no one is watching.
paragraphs.zh: 每个运动员背后都有一支团队：教练、医生、家人和朋友。他们开车送运动员去清晨训练，做饭，在糟糕的一天后给予安慰。然而站在起跑线上时，运动员是独自一人。这就是为什么那些安静的付出很重要。观众可以欢呼，却不能替你迈出最后一步。运动员必须一次又一次地决定，在无人注视时也到场。

paragraphs.en: The word sacrifice is often used in sports. It can mean missing a party, giving up a holiday, or saying no to late-night games. But athletes rarely describe it that way. They talk about love for the sport, about small improvements, and about teammates who depend on them. The sacrifice is real, but it is also mixed with joy.
paragraphs.zh: “牺牲”这个词在体育中常被使用。它可以指错过聚会、放弃假期，或拒绝深夜娱乐。但运动员很少这样描述。他们谈的是对这项运动的热爱、小小的进步，以及依赖他们的队友。牺牲是真实的，但也与快乐交织在一起。

paragraphs.en: So the next time you watch a medal ceremony, look beyond the shining metal. Remember the empty pool at 5 a.m., ice packs, the notebook of small goals, and the thousand silent choices. Success on the field may look like a sudden flash. In truth, it is built slowly, one unseen morning at a time. And that is the quiet lesson athletes teach us: the crowd sees the result, but the athlete lives the work.
paragraphs.zh: 所以下次你观看颁奖仪式时，请看向闪亮金属之外。记住清晨五点的空泳池、冰袋、记着小目标的笔记本，以及上千个无声的选择。赛场上的成功看起来像突然的闪光。事实上，它是缓慢建立的，一个又一个无人看见的清晨。这就是运动员教给我们的安静一课：观众看到结果，而运动员活在付出之中。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Athletes become famous mainly because of television.
The success of athletes depends on long, unseen effort and recovery.
Swimming is the hardest sport in the world.
Coaches and families are more important than athletes.
questions.explain: 文章主旨是运动员的成功来自长期看不见的重复训练、恢复和心理坚持，而不是电视或单项运动。

questions.q: According to the passage, why can a tiny technical change matter?
options: It can decide the difference between first and fourth place.
It makes the crowd cheer louder.
It reduces the cost of training.
questions.explain: 第二段指出，0.05秒的微小改进在顶级比赛中可能决定第一名和第四名的差别。

questions.q: What can be inferred about the runner who broke her foot?
options: She gave up running for good.
She found recovery boring but useless.
She rebuilt her ability step by step with small goals.
She depended only on her coach to recover.
questions.explain: 第五段说她用笔记本记录小目标，从站立、走路到慢跑，说明她靠逐步积累恢复能力。

questions.q: The word 'sacrifice' in paragraph 7 is closest in meaning to ______.
options: something given up for a goal
questions.explain: 第七段中sacrifice指为了运动目标而放弃聚会、假期等，因此最接近“为目标而舍弃的东西”。
